label: At HEAD the six runtimes fall into three delivery-proof classes: proven (claude 24/24, devin 24/24, pi 24/24, dsh 23/23 stored sessions), unproven (opencode 24/24 deliveryUnknown because the plugin pushes to output.system in memory with no store trace), and absent (codex 0/24, hooks unapproved).

The bytes the reader receives are identical across the hook and the OpenCode plugin on all nine committed probe prompts: one system entry each, 244 to 305 bytes, after rank 4 removed the duplicate compiled-routing line.
Codex is the only runtime where the reader receives no brief at all, still 0 of 24; this is the operator-owned hook approval already recorded in the goal log, not a code defect.

OpenCode's reader experience is truncated by the turn cap more than any other runtime: 8 of 24 runs exit 143, 6 of 14 offers land on a capped row, and its start rate is computed on only 5 of 12 start rows, so the published 2 of 5 understates what the reader was shown.

DSH's one unscored row is the one DSH line whose locator is null in the stale pre-015 arm; the other 23 lines carry a locator and delivered true, so it is a re-score artifact rather than a current delivery gap.
